module_title: Dimensional Analysis and Principle of Homogeneity
introduction: This is the most critical topic for advanced exams (NDA, CDS, RRB JE). Dimensional analysis is a mathematical tool used to check the correctness of physical equations and derive relationships between different quantities.

core_concepts.title: What is a Dimensional Formula?
core_concepts.description:
It is an expression that shows which fundamental quantities are present in a derived quantity. We use square brackets and capital letters: Mass $[M]$, Length $[L]$, and Time $[T]$. 
Example: Velocity = Distance / Time = $L / T$. So, its dimensional formula is $[M^0 L^1 T^{-1}]$.

core_concepts.title: Crucial Dimensional Formulas to Memorize
core_concepts.description:
1. Force: $[M^1 L^1 T^{-2}]$ (Mass $\times$ Acceleration) 
2. Work / Energy: $[M^1 L^2 T^{-2}]$ (Force $\times$ Distance) 
3. Power: $[M^1 L^2 T^{-3}]$ (Work / Time) 
4. Pressure / Stress: $[M^1 L^{-1} T^{-2}]$ (Force / Area).

core_concepts.title: Dimensionless Quantities
core_concepts.description:
Some physical quantities are ratios of two identical quantities. They have NO units and NO dimensions $[M^0 L^0 T^0]$. 
Examples: Strain (change in length / original length), Refractive Index, Relative Density, and Plane Angle.

core_concepts.title: Principle of Homogeneity
core_concepts.description: This principle states that you can only add or subtract physical quantities if they have the EXACT SAME dimensions. (You cannot add 5 kilograms to 10 meters). Therefore, in any correct physics equation (like $v = u + at$), every single term must have the same dimensional formula.

important_entities.name: Universal Gravitational Constant (G)
important_entities.significance:
From Newton's law $F = G(m_1 m_2)/r^2$, we get $G = (F \cdot r^2) / (m_1 \cdot m_2)$. 
Substituting dimensions: $([M L T^{-2}] \cdot [L^2]) / [M^2]$. 
Resulting Dimension of G: $[M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2}]$.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Examiners love asking 'Which pair has the same dimensional formula?' 
Memorize these pairs: 
1. Work, Energy, and Torque -> $[M L^2 T^{-2}]$ 
2. Pressure, Stress, and Modulus of Elasticity -> $[M L^{-1} T^{-2}]$ 
3. Impulse and Momentum -> $[M L T^{-1}]$.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation:
If you memorize Force ($MLT^{-2}$), you can derive almost anything. 
Want Work? Multiply Force by L -> $ML^2T^{-2}$. 
Want Pressure? Divide Force by L^2 -> $ML^{-1}T^{-2}$.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever asked to find the unit or dimension of a complex constant (like Planck's constant 'h' or Gravitational constant 'G'), do not panic. Write down its basic formula, substitute the units of the individual components, and solve it like basic algebra.
